question_text: A 72-year-old and his caregiver present for a follow-up after a transthoracic needle biopsy of one of the large lesions in his chest was reported as non-small cell carcinoma of the lung. Question: A 72-year-old and his caregiver present for a follow-up after a transthoracic needle biopsy of one of the large lesions in his chest was reported as non-small cell carcinoma of the lung. Previously, a chest CT revealed numerous nodules in the lungs bilaterally. The chest CT was ordered after the patient experienced a persistent cough with hemoptysis and a history of multiple episodes of pneumonia over the past year. The patient has a history of dementia and is a poor historian. The caregiver states that the patient has no history of smoking and that he was a lawyer before he retired, 10 years ago. The caregiver can only provide a limited medical history, but states that the patient sees another doctor “to monitor his prostate”. Which of the following is true regarding the pathogenesis of the nodules seen in this patient?

opb. Malignant transformation of neuroendocrine cells
opc. Infection of the lung parenchyma with a gram-negative bacteria grown on charcoal yeast agar
opd. Proliferation of cells that contain glands that produce mucin
ope. Tumors seeded via the pulmonary arteries
